Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:10:1.hebrew: דיקא נמי - דמתניתין לאו אהזאה וקידוש קאי, דקתני מי חטאת ואפר חטאת, שעדיין אינן מעורבין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:10:1.english: [The wording] is also precise - That our Mishnah does not refer to sprinkling and sanctification, as it teaches "water of purification and ashes of purification," which are not yet mixed together:

Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:12:1.hebrew: האומר מקודשת ואינה מקודשת - לשניהם — דאסורה לשניהם, אלא אם כן נתן האחד גט; ולאדם אחר אסורה, עד שיתנו שניהם גט. ובגמרא פליגי בה, ומפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:12:1.english: [HaOmer:] She is betrothed and not betrothed - [This means] to both of them, for she is forbidden to both of them unless one [of them] gives a bill of divorce, and to another man she is forbidden until both of them give a bill of divorce. And in the Gemara, [the Sages] disagree about it, and [the Gemara] explains the reasoning.

Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:12:2.hebrew: בת ישראל לכהן לא תאכל בתרומה - שמא אינן קדושין. ובת כהן לישראל נמי לא תאכל בתרומת בית אביה — שמא הוו קידושין, וזר פוסל בקדושין את בת כהן מן התרומה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:12:2.english: An Israelite woman [betrothed] to a priest may not partake of teruma - Lest they are not [valid] betrothals. And the daughter of a priest [betrothed] to an Israelite also may not partake of the teruma of her father's house — lest they were [valid] betrothals, and a non-priest disqualifies the daughter of a priest from teruma through betrothal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:13:1.hebrew: האומר מקודשת ואינה מקודשת - לשניהם, דאסורה לשניהם אלא אם כן נתן האחד גט, ולאדם אחר אסורה עד שיתנו שניהם גט. ובגמרא פליגי בה ומפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:13:1.english: [In the case of] one who says: "She is betrothed and not betrothed" - [This means] to both of them; for she is forbidden to both of them unless one [of them] gives [her] a bill of divorce, and to another man she is forbidden until both of them give [her] a bill of divorce. And in the Gemara, they disagree about it and [the Gemara] explains the reasoning:

Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:13:2.hebrew: בת ישראל לכהן לא תאכל בתרומה - שמא אינן קדושין. ובת כהן לישראל נמי לא תאכל בתרומת בית אביה, שמא הוו קידושין, וזר פוסל בקדושין את בת כהן מן התרומה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:13:2.english: The daughter of an Israelite [betrothed] to a priest may not partake of teruma - Lest it is not a [valid] betrothal. And the daughter of a priest [betrothed] to an Israelite also may not partake of the teruma of her father’s house, lest it was a [valid] betrothal, and a non-priest disqualifies the daughter of a priest from teruma through betrothal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:1:1.hebrew: הוצאה את, הוא סבר: משמעתא קאמר ליה - מוצא את משמועה זו, נראה שאין אתה חכם בה. אי נמי: קטיל קני באגמא את — לשון "הוצא ודפנא" (סוכה דף כג.):
Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:1:1.english: “You are a hutza’a”; he thought he was speaking to him regarding the halakhic teaching - You are removed from this teaching; it appears that you are not knowledgeable in it. Alternatively: You are a cutter of reeds in the marsh [i.e., an unlearned person] — an expression [related to] “palm branches and laurel” (Sukkah 23a).

Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:2:1.english: Let us say [it is a dispute between] tanna’im - [Whether] the benefit of discretion has monetary value or does not have monetary value.

Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:2:2.english: He pays him the value of his untithed produce - Even the value of the teruma and tithe that it contains.

Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:2:3.hebrew: אלא דמי חולין שבו - אבל בתרומה ומעשר, אמר ליה: "לאו בעל דברים דידי את". וכשיבא כהן גם הוא לתובעו, ידחהו ויאמר: "לא לך אתננה, כי אם לכהן אחר":
Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:2:3.english: Only the value of the non-sacred [produce] that it contains - But regarding the terumah and the tithe, [the thief] can say to him: “You are not my litigant.” And when a priest also comes to claim it from him, he will rebuff him and say: “I will not give it to you, but rather to another priest.”

Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:3:1.hebrew: ה"ג לא דכ"ע טובת הנאה אינה ממון והכא במתנות שלא הורמו קמיפלגי - וכגון שנפל לו טבל זה מבית אבי אמו כהן. רבי סבר: כמי שהורמו דמיין, וזכה אבי אמו בתרומה ומעשרות שבו — שאף מעשר ראשון לכהנים, מדקנסינהו עזרא ללוים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:3:1.english: This is the reading: "No, everyone agrees that the benefit of discretion does not have monetary value, and here they disagree regarding gifts that have not been separated" - And [this is a case] where this untithed produce fell to him [as an inheritance] from the household of his mother’s father, a priest. Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] holds: They are considered as though they have been separated, and his mother’s father acquired the teruma and the tithes within it — for even the first tithe [goes] to the priests, since Ezra penalized the Levites.

Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:3:2.hebrew: ורבי יוסי סבר לאו כמי שהורמו דמיין - וצריך היורש הזה לתתן לכהן, ואין לו בהן אלא טובת הנאה, והיא אינה ממון:
Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:3:2.english: And Rabbi Yose holds [that they are] not considered as though they have been separated - And this heir must give them to a priest, and he has in them only the benefit of discretion, and it does not have monetary value.

Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:4:1.hebrew: ואיבעית אימא דכ"ע כמי שהורמו דמיין וטובת הנאה אינה ממון - והכא לאו דנפלו לו מבית אבי אמו כהן עסקינן, אלא שגדלו בארצו. וטעמא דרבי משום דאית ליה דשמואל, דאמר: חטה אחת פוטרת את הכרי. הילכך, אמר ליה בעל הטבל אל הגנב: כולה דידי הוא, דפטרנא נפשי בחטה אחת לתרומה. וכי פליג רבי עליה דר' יוסי בר' יהודה, בתרומה לחודה פליג; אבל במעשר מודה, דלאו בעל דברים דידיה הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:4:1.english: And if you wish, say that everyone agrees that they are considered as though they have been separated, and the benefit of discretion does not have monetary value - And here, it is not [a case where produce] fell to him from the household of his mother’s father, a priest, that we are dealing with, but rather [produce] that grew on his own land. And the reasoning of Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] is because he holds in accordance with [the opinion of] Shmuel, who said: One grain exempts the [entire] heap. Therefore, the owner of the untithed produce can say to the thief: “It is all mine, for I can discharge my obligation with one grain for teruma.” And when Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] disagrees with Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, he disagrees only concerning teruma; but concerning tithe he concedes that he is not his legal adversary [to claim it from him].

Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:5:1.hebrew: ורבי יוסי לית ליה דשמואל - הילכך, בתרומה נמי לא מצי תבע ליה. וה"ה דמצי לאוקמיה נמי בטבלים שנפלו לו, ודכ"ע כמי שלא הורמו דמיין, וטובת הנאה אינה ממון, וקמיפלגי בדשמואל. אלא אי אוקמת הכי, אוקמת ליה מתניתין, דקתני "מקודשת", דלא כתרוייהו; דכיון דטובת הנאה אינה ממון ומתנות שלא הורמו כלא הורמו דמיין, היכי מיקדשא? הא אין לו בתרומה אלא טובת הנאה, ואפילו נפלו לו טבלים מבית אבי אמו כהן! אבל השתא דאמרינן כמי שהורמו דמיין, ופלוגתייהו בטיבלא דאתי מארעיה — מתרצא מתני' כדשנינן לעיל, ודברי הכל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:5:1.english: And Rabbi Yosei does not hold in accordance with Shmuel - Therefore, regarding the teruma as well, [the owner] cannot claim [its value] from him. And likewise, [the Gemara] could also have established [the dispute] in [a case of] untithed produce that fell to him [as an inheritance from his maternal grandfather, a priest], where everyone agrees that [unseparated gifts] are considered as though they have not been separated, and the benefit of discretion is not monetary [property], and they disagree regarding [the statement] of Shmuel. However, if you were to establish it in this way, you would establish our Mishnah, which teaches: "[She is] betrothed," as not [being] in accordance with either of them; for since the benefit of discretion is not monetary [property] and gifts that have not been separated are considered as though they have not been separated, how could she be betrothed? Behold, he has nothing in the teruma other than the benefit of discretion, even if untithed produce fell to him from the household of his mother’s father, a priest! However, now that we say [everyone agrees that they] are considered as though they have been separated, and their dispute is regarding untithed produce that came from his [own] land, the Mishnah is resolved as we answered above, and [it is] universally agreed upon.

Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:6:1.hebrew: קנסוהו לגנב - שלא תהא תרומה אצלו ממון שאין לו תובעים, ונמצא חוטא נשכר:
Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:6:1.english: They penalized the thief - So that the *teruma* should not be in his possession property that has no claimants, and [thus] a sinner would profit.

Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:8:1.hebrew: להזות ולקדש - משנה היא בבכורות: הנוטל שכרו לדון — דיניו בטלים, להזות ולקדש — מימיו מי מערה, ואפרו אפר מקלה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:8:1.english: To sprinkle and to sanctify - It is a Mishnah in Bekhorot: One who accepts payment to judge, his judgments are nullified; to sprinkle and to sanctify, his water is cave water, and his ashes are ordinary ashes.

Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:8:2.hebrew: להזות - על הטמא. ולקדש מי חטאת — כשנותן האפר במים, קרי קדושה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:8:2.english: To sprinkle - Upon the impure [person]. And to sanctify purification water — when one places the ashes into the water, [it] is called "sanctification."

Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:8:4.hebrew: אפר מקלה - כלומר, סתם אפר שבא מן הקלוי באש:
Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:8:4.english: Burnt ashes - That is to say, ordinary ash that comes from [something] roasted in fire.

Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:9:1.hebrew: בשכר הבאה - האפר ממקום למקום, ושכר מילוי המים — דמילתא דטירחא היא, ורחמנא לא רמיא עליה, ושרי למשקל אגרא, ומקודשת. ומתניתין דבכורות — בשכר הזאה וקידוש, דליכא טירחא, ושכר לימוד מצוה הוא נוטל; והתורה אמרה (דברים ד׳:ה׳) ראה למדתי אתכם וגו' כאשר צוני וגו' — מה אני בחנם, אף אתם בחנם (נדרים דף לז.):
Rashi on Kiddushin 58b:9:1.english: With payment for bringing - The ashes from place to place, and payment for drawing the water — for it is a matter of exertion, and the Merciful One did not impose [it] upon him [as an obligation], so it is permitted to take a wage, and she is betrothed. And the mishna in Bekhorot [is dealing with] payment for sprinkling and sanctifying, where there is no exertion, and [thus] he is taking payment for teaching a mitzvah; and the Torah said (Deuteronomy 4:5): "Behold, I have taught you, etc., as [the Lord my God] commanded me, etc." — just as I [did so] for free, so too you [must do so] for free (Nedarim 37a).

Tosafot on Kiddushin 58b:12:1.hebrew: מתני': האומר - והלך וקידשה לעצמו מקודשת. וא"ת: מה חידוש יש כאן? פשיטא! ויש לומר: דמיירי כגון דאמר השליח לאשה בשעת קדושין: "פלוני שלחני לקדשך לו", ובתוך כך אמר לה: "הרי את מקודשת לי", והיא ידעה דקידשה לנפשיה, דאל"כ לא היתה מקודשת לו. ואשמועינן חידוש, דמהו דתימא: הא דקאמר "לי", לצורך משלחו קאמר? קמ"ל דלא:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 58b:12:1.english: Mishnah: One who says - "And went and betrothed her to himself, she is betrothed." And if you say: What novelty is there here? It is obvious! And one can say that it is dealing with [a case] where the agent said to the woman at the time of betrothal: "So-and-so sent me to betroth you to him," and in the midst of this he said to her: "You are hereby betrothed to me," and she knew that he was betrothing her for himself, as if not so, she would not have been betrothed to him. And [the Mishnah] teaches us a novelty, for lest you say: That which he said, "to me," he meant on behalf of his sender? It teaches us that [this is] not so.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 58b:8:1.hebrew: מימיו מי מערה - פי' בקונטרס: מים סרוחים. ובחנם דחק לפרש כן, דמצי לפרש מי מערה ממש, כלומר: מכונסים, ואינן מים חיים, ואנן מים חיים בעינן. ואפרו אפר מקלה — פירוש: שעבר על דברי תורה, דכתיב (דברים ד׳:ה׳): "ראה למדתי אתכם חוקים ומשפטים" — מה אני בחנם, אף אתם בחנם; וזה שעשה בשכר עבר על דברי תורה. ומקרא ממש לא נפק ליה, דהא לא שמעינן מיניה היכא דעבד בשכר דלא מהני; אלא אסמכתא בעלמא הוא, דלא מהני אפילו דיעבד:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 58b:8:1.english: "His water is cave water" - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: Foul water. But he strained unnecessarily to explain [it] so, as he could have explained [it as] actual cave water — that is to say, gathered [standing] water, which is not living water, and we require living water. And [regarding] "and his ash is burnt ash" — the explanation is that he transgressed the words of the Torah, as it is written (Deuteronomy 4:5): "See, I have taught you statutes and ordinances" — just as I [taught] for free, so too you [must act] for free; and this person who acted for payment transgressed the words of the Torah. And it is not literally derived from the verse [that the act is invalid], for we do not learn from it that where one acted for payment it is not effective; rather, [the verse] is merely an asmakhta [scriptural support] that it is not effective even post facto.
